entries.name: Golem domestique
entries.description: domestic golem, large round chunky gray-green patchwork stone/metal humanoid with small simple head, two tiny dot eyes, broad torso, huge rounded arms and mitten hands, beige strapped work apron, short block feet, gentle expression; no police cap. BALLMAN/goLEM palette is a game adaptation because source p65 is uncolored line art. Keep Elq fully clothed and innocent.
entries.prompt:
Production PIXEL ART for WordEnd HD-2D, not illustration. Crisp hand-placed square pixel clusters, stepped shading, limited desaturated autumn palette, hard dark-colored 1px contour (not pure black), absolutely NO smooth painting, NO anti-alias fringe, NO 3D rendering. Soft flat left lighting. Transparent PNG alpha. Exact PORTRAIT canvas 1024 x 1536; atlas SIX equal columns by TWELVE equal rows. Cell size about 170x128. One character with identical costume and scale across all 42 full-body frames. Small legible RPG figure 2.5-3 heads tall. Full figure incl feet/ears/horns and carried props fits inside every cell with transparent padding, max 105px high; never overlapping other cells. No visible grid, no labels/numbers/text, no background or floor or shadows. NO combat for this NPC. Camera straight-on slightly elevated 10degrees, not isometric. ROWS 1-4 STRICT FRONT facing viewer, rows5-8 STRICT BACK with NO face/eyes visible, rows9-12 STRICT RIGHT profile. Animation placement EACH FOUR-ROW GROUP: first row TWO idle frames in columns1-2 only; other4cells EMPTY transparent. Second row SIX alternating walk cycle frames in cols1-6. Third row FOUR running frames in cols1-4, other2 EMPTY. Fourth row TWO talking frames cols1-2 with small gesture and open/closed mouth, cells3-5 EMPTY, cell6 EMPTY except FINAL ROW12 col6 contains ONE close-up head-and-shoulders portrait turned three-quarter RIGHT. Entire atlas thus42 full-body frames +1portrait. Hands/feet alternate phases genuinely, standing feet same baseline; no duplicated columns substituting movement. Read reference image ONLY for identity, redesign as pixel art.
